newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon's property tax revenues rise in June.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon's property tax revenues rise in June.

text.p: Lebanese government revenues from taxation of property deals rose 10.48 percent in June over the same month last year, according to figures released by the finance ministry on Monday.
The ministry collected $13,943,110 compared with $12,620,998 in June 1996. It collected $14,128,131 in May.
Collected property tax revenues for the first six months of 1997 totalled $70,803,409 compared with $61,757,822 over the same period a year earlier -- a rise of 14.65 percent.
Tax rates on property deals vary from district to district, but average about 6.5 percent.
However, tax collection does not truly reflect the state of the market because deals are sometimes understated to avoid tax, property analysts say.
